detailHeading: What goes into a bathroom that lasts
detailBody: Most bathroom problems start with water getting where it should not. Before new tile or a new vanity goes in, Keith checks the subfloor, the wall behind the tub or shower, the shut-off valves and the exhaust fan.

Georgian Bay homes and cottages see damp summers and cold winters. A fan that vents outside, a waterproof membrane behind shower tile and good caulking at every joint keep moisture out of the walls and stop mould before it starts.

If you are planning ahead, tell Keith how long you plan to stay in the home and who uses the bathroom. A grab bar blocking in the wall now, or a shower with a low curb, costs little during a renovation and saves a second job later.

faqs.q: Can you work with my existing layout?
faqs.a: Yes. Many bathroom updates keep the toilet, sink and shower where they are, which keeps the work simpler. If you want to move a fixture, Keith will look at the plumbing and talk through what is involved.
Your estimate depends on the work, the materials and the condition of the space. Discuss the details with Keith and review the estimate before approving the project.
Where a job needs a licensed plumber or electrician, that requirement is identified in the estimate and coordinated with a licensed trade.

faqs.q: How is waterproofing handled in a shower?
faqs.a: Tiled showers go over a waterproof membrane before any tile is set. It is the part you never see, and the part that protects the walls and floor behind the tile.
Yes. Keith works on homes and cottages. Let him know if the property is seasonal, how to access it and any timing you need to plan around.
